High-quality optics, two trapping lasers at different wavelengths, and careful control of losses during rearrangement yield arrays of up to 1024 atoms, with trapping lifetimes near 5000 seconds. The long lifetimes and clean arrays open room for both analog and digital quantum work with Rydberg states, where atoms are excited to highly energetic orbits.
arxiv-2604-07405: Medeiros asks why gradient descent finds good solutions in non-convex neural net training despite worst-case hardness. For gradient flow on bias-free ReLU nets, he shows L minus 1 conservation laws trap paths on lower-dimensional manifolds, balancing squared norms across adjacent layers. Discrete descent breaks these laws, with drift growing as step size to a power near 1.1 to 1.6 by architecture, loss, and width. He derives an exact spectral formula for drift, checked in 23 tests, and finds two regimes split by a width-dependent edge-of-stability transition.
arxiv-2604-07805: Morita and 14 colleagues map the electronic structure of CsBi2, a superconductor whose bismuth atoms form a three-dimensional pyrochlore network. Strong spin-orbit coupling shapes its states. Photoemission measurements plus first-principles calculations reveal a flat band with p-orbital character near the U-K line. Type-I and type-II saddle points linked by a flat band also pile up electron states near the Fermi level. Together, multiple singularities with nontrivial topology suggest a new route to interaction-driven quantum phases.
arxiv-2604-07905: Nakatsuyama and Takahashi study linked curves of regular plane curves and Legendre curves alike. As linked curves they consider Bertrand regular plane curves and Bertrand Legendre curves, including parallel, evolute, and involute curves plus evolutoid and involutoid curves. Linked curves may develop singular points even when the original curve is regular, and Legendre curves give a fitting framework for study. The paper gives existence conditions for Bertrand families, an inverse operation for Bertrand Legendre curves, and a mapping between Legendre curve sets that proves bijective up to equivalence.
arxiv-2604-08005: Seip and Hein introduce PRAC, an attack on computer use agents that shifts focus rather than aiming at model output. These agents work with visual interfaces, doing complex tasks but opening new security holes. Prior work focused on the language modality, leaving vision less studied. PRAC shifts the model's internal preferences by steering focus toward a stealthy adversarial patch. The team shows it can push a shopping agent's choice toward a chosen target product. White-box access is needed, marking a limit on its real-world reach.
arxiv-2604-08105: Topolnicki and five colleagues offer direction-aware traits for elastic stiffness tensors of porous matter. Old traits from topological data analysis stay the same under swaps of spatial axes. They therefore cannot show load axis, which matters for uneven stress response. The new method embeds the loading axis into filter functions used to compute lasting homology and Euler curves. Applied to porous microstructures, axis-aware traits plus networks trained on voxel shapes predict the full stiffness tensor, with similar results on main one-axis, Poisson, and shear parts.
arxiv-2604-08205: Bienkowski and four colleagues consider how many transactions a channel in a payment channel network can accept. Payment channel networks promise faster, more scalable cryptocurrency transactions. At their core, these networks route transactions through intermediary channels, not the blockchain. A channel forwards a transaction only when it holds enough funds, so balance is a current bottleneck for throughput. Earlier work either solved the optimization problem with every transaction known in advance or tested heuristics on datasets. This work considers the purely online version.
arxiv-2604-09005: Dresselhaus and five colleagues review textiles as mechanical metamaterials, a corner of condensed matter physics that the field long ignored. Starting from spun yarn and its basic model, they trace twisted bundles through woven and knitted cloth. The review covers the symmetry, topology, and mechanics of these fabrics, showing how plain cloth embodies deep structure. They have existed through most of human history, yet remain a little-studied corner of the field.
arxiv-2604-09605: Park, Park, and Lim reframe human-AI interaction traces as creative artifacts rather than audit trails. Disclosure of how much an AI wrote, they note, treats collaboration as a matter of counting and surveillance. Drawing on blackout poetry, they instead present AI output as found material, over which writers inscribe their own curation and reinterpretation. Designed as aesthetic objects, traces could help readers appreciate and trust the writer's creative contribution instead of merely tallying machine involvement.
arxiv-2604-09705: Cruzes offers a sustainability-bound control method for self-run AI setup, where energy, cooling, and links bind daily work tightly. Carbon load, water usage, and power limits enter as strict constraints rather than tunable costs. Compute siting and optical network routing are jointly tuned in one closed-loop system. The Feasible Sovereign Operating Region maps which workloads a system can sustain, and tests show joint tuning beating older methods on impact. Infeasibility events read not as solver faults but as signals that spending or less work is needed.
arxiv-2604-09805: Pinto and three co-authors introduce CodeGen, Zup's internal coding agent, and argue that model quality alone cannot carry a demo into live use. Tool design, safety checks, state handling, and trust tuning prove equally key, yet rarely noted. Focused tool design, such as string-swap edits over full-file redrafts, and layered guardrails did more for reliability than prompt engineering. Stepwise review modes drove organic uptake without forcing trust. The work choices around the model, not the model itself, decide whether a coding agent gives real value.
arxiv-2604-09905: Yang and Mitr tackle pediatric triage, where models lean too hard on structured vitals and collapse when notes matter most. Their late-fusion model runs tabular vitals through XGBoost and clinical text through Bio_ClinicalBERT, joined by a logistic regression meta-classifier predicting the Emergency Severity Index. Trained only on adult cases from MIMIC-IV and NHAMCS, it is tested zero-shot on children, with dropout blocking adult-specific overfitting. A 30 to 40 percent dropout rate lifts the pediatric Quadratic Weighted Kappa to 0.351, showing dropout curbs collapse and aids generalization.
arxiv-2604-10005: Dalen designs a study for institutional liquidity entering prediction markets, now resembling electronic markets. The paper defines a market-quality lens, separates the main entry channels, and maps identification problems. A synthetic laboratory serves as proof of concept for the measurement pipeline. Its narrow lesson: coverage, incentives, and automation need not share one channel. Average gains need not reach all traders equally. The sharpest losses likely hit shock states, when slow takers receive the least pass-through. The synthetic results stress-test the design without settling the live question.
arxiv-2604-10305: Kyem, Asamoah, and Aboah propose class-tuned cooperative view for many-class 3D object detection from LiDAR. Most joint finders fuse all classes alike, missing the shape of small and large objects, and narrow tests stress single classes. Their model joins multi-size window focus with scale routing, split fusion for small and large objects, top boost, and even weighting. On the benchmark across five teamwork settings, it beats middle rivals, with the largest gains on trucks, clear gains on walkers, and close results on cars.
arxiv-2604-10605: Pochekutov studies the diagonal of a Laurent series for a rational function in several complex variables. The diagonal is the series formed by matching powers across all variables. When the denominator behaves well against its Newton polyhedron, he proves the diagonal extends along paths in a complex torus. Each path must avoid a set spelled out in advance, the Landau variety, built from discriminants tied to faces of that polyhedron.
arxiv-2604-10905: Ghosh and seventeen colleagues present Audio Flamingo Next (AF-Next), the strongest audio-language model of the Audio Flamingo line for speech, sounds, and music. Against Audio Flamingo 3, it adds a stronger base model, data plans, long-audio support to 30 minutes, and Temporal Audio Chain-of-Thought, grounding reasoning steps to timestamps. The team scaled datasets past 1 million hours, training across pre-training, mid-training, and post-training. Across 20 benchmarks, AF-Next beats open models by wide margins and rivals far larger open and closed models, with three variants open.
arxiv-2604-11005: Zuo and three colleagues propose Diffusion-CAM, the first clarity method built for diffusion multimodal large language models. These models generate tokens by joint cleaning, giving smooth, spread patterns across the sequence, unlike autoregressive models with ordered activations. Existing class mapping methods suit local, ordered links and fit these behaviours poorly. Diffusion-CAM derives raw activation maps by probing middle model states in a gradient-based way, catching latent features and their class-specific gradients. Four modules resolve spatial blur and ease intra-image confounds in noisy signals.
arxiv-2604-11105: Lee, Ryu, and Yun widen a classic fast method, Nesterov acceleration, beyond smooth convex problems. Their method, NOD, splits an operator into two parts, one cyclically monotone and one plainly monotone, using the tightest such split, the Asplund split, to drive the steps. The work recovers the classic theory and gives a new bound on the steps needed to reach an accurate solution of strongly monotone, Lipschitz operator problems.
arxiv-2604-11205: Biró studies the local square mean in the hyperbolic circle problem, which counts orbit points inside a hyperbolic circle of radius R. A known estimate carries error e to the two-thirds R, unimproved for any group. For the modular group with coincident points, earlier work gave an exponent of nine-fourteenths for the local L2 error norm, beating the pointwise bound. Here Biró improves that exponent further, conditionally on a twisted Linnik-Selberg-type conjecture for sums of Salié sums.
arxiv-2604-11505: Zhang and Lu prove a stability result for the anti-Ramsey number of matchings. Take an edge-colored complete graph with at least g(n,s) colors and no rainbow matching of size s+2. Then it must contain a monochromatic complete graph on n-s vertices, or a monochromatic join of a complete graph on n-2s-1 vertices with an independent set on 2s+1 vertices. The result pins down the near-extremal structures for matchings.
arxiv-2604-11705: Prahlad, Fan, and Kim propose a reactor-model approach, realized by the open-source Lingua Franca framework, for agentic AI-powered human-in-the-loop cyber-physical systems. Agents interact with physical settings and human users, but unpredictable humans, agents, and changing settings create nondeterminism. The Lingua Franca approach restores determinism, demonstrated through an agentic driving coach case study. Evaluating it surfaces challenges in restoring determinism and pathways to address them.
arxiv-2604-11905: Powley, Smethurst, Lintott, and Géron introduce a kinematic disturbance measure, DVSG, that compares a galaxy's stellar and gas velocity maps from IFS. It aims to catch disturbances other methods miss while limiting bias toward galaxy traits or data quirks. Applied to hidden active galactic nuclei in the MaNGA survey, it finds no clear gap between active galaxies and a matched control set of inactive ones. That suggests AGN triggering needs no special disturbance beyond what inactive galaxies show.
arxiv-2604-12505: E. Javier Olucha and three colleagues model fuel sloshing in spacecraft tanks. Sloshing fuel complicates test campaigns for spacecraft. Their first step is an open, fast, two-dimensional tank simulator built in Python with Jax. It runs on graphics chips in parallel and supports auto differentiation. Next, they build surrogate models from simulator input-output data. The surrogate uses a linear parameter-varying state-space form. Closed-loop tests show it runs two orders of magnitude faster than the full model.
arxiv-2604-12705: Sedighe Sajadian and Man Ho Chan evaluate self-lensing in white dwarf binaries. Companions are neutron stars or black holes in edge-on orbits. Detectability is tested for TESS and Roman. Neutron star systems under 25 days show large sources, while black hole systems over 3 days show smaller ones. Signal odds run near one in a thousand and one in a hundred, best for low-mass white dwarfs around massive companions. Detectable signals need fitting periods, strong signals, and coverage. TESS may catch at least one signal, while Roman catches none.
arxiv-2604-13005: Hearn determines exactly when two finite graphs share the same Bell colouring graph, whose vertices partition a graph's vertices into independent sets. He shows every n-vertex graph with no vertex of degree n minus 1 is fixed by its Bell colouring graph. The upper-Bell version fixes it too when k is at most n minus 2. Graphs of low maximum degree are fixed by the Bell k-colouring graph when k exceeds the chromatic number; complements restate this for cliques.
arxiv-2604-13105: Toro recalls the Russian mathematician Sergey Godunov, whose daughter asked him to contribute to a book about her father's life. Their link began at a Lake Tahoe conference in 1995, then meetings in Novosibirsk, Manchester, Oxford, and Cambridge, plus briefer encounters in France and Russia. The notes trace Godunov's mathematical creativity across many branches of science and its lasting influence on generations of mathematicians in academia and industry.
arxiv-2604-13205: Radhakrishnan, Chakraborty, and Mathur present a lattice quantum chromodynamics study of heavy baryons containing charm and bottom quarks, treating all valence quarks relativistically. Using 2+1+1 HISQ ensembles at the physical point, they compute ground-state energies of spin-3/2 positive-parity baryons, singly, doubly, and triply heavy. The work is the first to investigate heavy baryons with fully relativistic bottom quarks.
arxiv-2604-13305: Magid and six colleagues audit reward models used in text-to-image generation for demographic bias. Reward models score outputs, filter datasets, guide training, and screen finished images, yet their fairness as scoring tools was largely untested. The audit finds these models encode demographic bias, so reward-guided tuning tends to sexualize female subjects, reinforce gender and racial stereotypes, and shrink demographic diversity. The authors call for better data collection and training.
arxiv-2604-13405: Rudrasamudram and Malaichamee give a unified survey of singularity avoidance in inverse kinematics for serial robot arms. Singular poses cut mobility, send joint speeds sky high, and break solvers, yet no prior survey bridges classical singularity-robust methods with learning-based ones. Their taxonomy sorts methods by the geometry they keep and by formal versus tested guarantees, and they propose a benchmarking protocol. Tests of 12 solvers on the Franka Panda show pure learning tools fail even on easy targets, while hybrid warm-start designs save them with classical refinement.
arxiv-2604-13705: Chaki, Gourru, and Velcin ask whether fairness can emerge from agents talking to each other, rather than from one centrally tuned model. In a hospital triage setup, two agents negotiate over three debate rounds. One follows an ethical framework via retrieval, while the other is unaligned or biased toward demographic groups. Neither agent alone allocates fairly, yet their joint final allocation can meet fairness criteria. Aligned agents partly correct bias through contestation, not override.
arxiv-2604-14105: Ony gives axioms for the algebraic theory of right-preordered groups and preordered groups. He then studies lattices of effective equivalence relations in that setting. The paper proves the category of right-preordered groups is S-protomodular for Schreier split epimorphisms and action representable over that class. It defines S-precrossed and S-crossed modules, matching them to Schreier internal reflexive graphs and categories, and picks out groupoids among the latter.
arxiv-2604-14205: Hengster-Movrić, Lehký, and Yaghmaie design cooperative protocols for multi-agent systems whose agents hold only finite states. Both scalar single-integrator consensus and general linear time-invariant synchronization come under study. Finite-state agents, with tiny memory reading a finite alphabet, resist communication noise well, but building an admissible communication topology is NP-hard. The authors explore subsets of admissible graph matrices and offer two new algorithms to build them, with simulations backing the approach.
arxiv-2604-14305: Talbot, Kotlar, and Ke combine Bayesian and frequentist methods for per-gene promises in copy number variation tests. Even robust Bayesian credible ranges miss the mark badly on panels with few amplicons per gene. Their hybrid framework scores Bayesian posterior functionals on validation samples and fits squared losses to a Gamma distribution, yielding tolerance ranges with valid frequentist coverage. Imputation, regularization, and evidence-based stratification make the method practical. Tests on two panels show single-digit mean absolute coverage error, versus above 60 percent for Bayesian comparators on ERBB2.
arxiv-2604-14505: Hsiao, Yuan, and Wan examine Hayward-like regular black hole lensing versus Schwarzschild. In weak fields, bending gains a small positive correction growing with mass times core scale squared over impact parameter cubed. Light bends slightly more than Schwarzschild, negligibly at large impact parameters. Galaxy-scale Einstein-ring data cannot yet pin down the regular-core scale. Toward Sagittarius A* and M87*, the asymptotic image position matches Schwarzschild. Yet the core scale shifts lensing coefficients, separations, flux ratios, and time delays, all consistent with current data.
arxiv-2604-15005: Tsuchiya studies the extreme case of Gorenstein simplices, geometric shapes tied to lattice points, where dimension equals twice the degree minus one. He describes these shapes exactly through even binary self-complementary codes, a coding-theory lens. Combined with known lists of reflexive shapes, the result classifies all such simplices of degree 3 and 4. The same work classifies a matching family of fake weighted projective spaces.
arxiv-2604-15105: Tang and colleagues study dense mixes of passive and active self-aligning disks, asking how the idle share steers order. The passive fraction drives an order-disorder shift that runs smooth when motion is uniform but jumps when motion is directional. A mean-field equation from the disks' heading dynamics captures both cases. Near the shift, ordered states can wobble or rotate through several long-lived patterns, shaped by idle-disk placement and lattice flaws.
arxiv-2604-15305: Ho disproves Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances in high dimensions, which asked whether point sets with all pairwise distances at least one apart must span nearly n squared. For every prime power q he builds q plus one points in a high-dimensional space whose distances stay separated yet whose diameter falls short of the conjectured bound. He formalizes the whole proof in Lean 4.
arxiv-2604-15505: Choi and four colleagues propose PolicyBank, a memory system that lets LLM agents refine their grasp of organizational policies through interaction and corrective feedback. Instead of treating policy text as fixed truth, it keeps structured tool-level insights and updates them, closing specification gaps that otherwise lock in compliant-but-wrong behavior. On a benchmark extended with controlled policy gaps, PolicyBank closes up to 82 percent of the gap to a human oracle.
arxiv-2604-15605: Tang and Deng propose an interference-interaction scheme for programmable few-photon emission from three atoms coupled to orthogonal cavity modes. Eliminating an auxiliary Fabry-Pérot cavity yields a tunable spin-exchange interaction carried by the cavity, which with a controllable geometric phase reshapes the dressed-state spectrum. Phase zero gives tunable one- and two-photon emission, while phase two-pi-over-three activates a resonant three-photon channel with much higher purity.
arxiv-2604-16005: Gazdzicki and 42 colleagues recap the ISO-BREAK 25 workshop on isospin-symmetry breaking, kaons and beyond, held at Jan Kochanowski University in Kielce on October 23 to 25, 2025. The report covers the isospin-symmetry breaking found by NA61/SHINE in nucleus-nucleus collisions at the CERN SPS, its backup by others, and studies in electron-positron and deep inelastic scattering. It also reviews theory and outlines priorities for experiments and theory for grasping this unexplained phenomenon.
arxiv-2604-16105: Byrne, Couvreur, and François study decoding algorithms for tensor codes, subspaces of higher-order tensors measured by tensor rank. They generalise a class introduced by Roth, whose decoding for low-rank errors can be extended at exponential cost in the decoding radius. Their work covers code properties and decoding under several metrics bounded by the tensor-rank metric. It offers a fibre-wise method, where each fibre acts as a Gabidulin codeword, and a generalisation of the Loidreau-Overbeck method tied to slice and fibre spaces.
arxiv-2604-16305: Hyrynsalmi, Brown, Serebrenik, Baltes, and Jaccheri examine political and ideological pressure on software engineering research, through cases of DEI backlash. Funding and guidance shifts, especially in the US, have rippled through the global research ecosystem, operating at macro, meso, and micro levels. Drawing on community survey responses and case examples, they show how these pressures affect software engineering research, despite a common belief that the field is politically and ideologically neutral.
arxiv-2604-16505: Varzaneh and colleagues predict which embryos will form blastocysts in IVF, a choice now driven by manual inspection of extensive time-lapse images. Many clinics lack full time-lapse systems, so only limited daily images exist. Their hybrid model pairs DINOv2, a vision transformer that extracts embryo image features, with an attention-based long short-term memory network that tracks development over time. Tested on 704 embryo videos, it reached about 96 percent accuracy, beating existing methods, and held up with missing frames, helping embryologists choose embryos with greater confidence.
arxiv-2604-17005: Liu and three colleagues give music-driven dance generation something it lacked: control through plain text. Their TeMuDance framework uses motion as a shared anchor to align separate music-dance and text-motion collections in one embedding space. A light text-control branch then trains atop a frozen music-to-dance diffusion backbone. Retrieved supervision is cleaned by dual-stream fine-tuning with confidence filtering, and a new task-aligned metric checks whether prompts produce the intended movements.
arxiv-2604-17105: Liao and Shi show that subword tokenization, which chops words without regard to sound, weakens how text-only language models encode sound knowledge. They introduce the syllabification-tokenization alignment distance, a metric for the mismatch between token boundaries and natural syllable boundaries, finding greater mismatch means poorer sound representations. A lightweight IPA-based fine-tuning method then infuses sound awareness, improving three sound-related tasks with only a 1.1 percent drop on GSM8K and a small drop on MMLU.
arxiv-2604-17605: Lindstrøm and eight colleagues describe an achromatic lattice for moving beams between plasma stages, built on the nonlinear plasma lens. High divergence and energy spread cause chromatic aberrations that block staging. The lattice preserves emittance for spreads up to several percent, with tunable R56 for bunch length or self-fix. Results are modeled on paper and in tests against a quadrupole-sextupole setup twice as long, with twice the parts and tighter bandwidth. Scaling to TeV levels follows a square-root length rule, with synchrotron light eased.
arxiv-2604-17705: Ginovyan surveys long-run variance of the best linear unbiased estimator, or BLUE, for the mean of stationary processes. That pattern follows model smoothness and memory, and is set solely by the spectrum near the origin. Where models are nondeterministic, BLUE variance behaves as a power, while for deterministic models it falls exponentially. Exponential decay to zero needs spectral density to vanish on a nonzero Lebesgue-measure set near zero. The survey also covers how well other linear methods do against the BLUE.
arxiv-2604-18005: Nuo Chen and seven colleagues study diversity in multi-agent systems for open-ended idea generation across model, agent, and system levels. At model level, stronger aligned models give less marginal diversity despite higher sample quality, a compute efficiency paradox. Authority dynamics suppress meaning diversity relative to junior groups, while larger groups yield less return and dense talk speeds early convergence. The authors attribute this diversity collapse mainly to interaction shape, not weak models, urging designs that preserve independence and disagreement.
arxiv-2604-18305: Tajeuna, Owusu, Brun, and Wang present CAARL, a language-model method for forecasting series that evolve together over time. CAARL splits each series into autoregressive pieces, builds a graph of time dependencies, and turns that graph into a narrative the model can read. The resulting chain-of-thought-like path links each forecast to explicit reasoning steps, keeping the process transparent. Tests on real data sets show competitive accuracy with state-of-the-art forecasters while adding interpretability.
arxiv-2604-18605: Grace Burtenshaw, Ashley Burtenshaw, and Carney seek what drives Australia's resilient, rising house prices. They model house price with a differential equation for intuition about its history and rate responsiveness. The model identifies a decoupling point between house price and mortgage rate, with supply limits the main driver. Extreme value techniques on real data show how rate effectiveness in moderating extreme prices changed before and after this decoupling. Without housing supply growth, through deregulation or less government-building competition, an 11 percent rate increase is required to slow extreme housing costs.
arxiv-2604-18705: Dey and four colleagues study a tiny spin-1 model on the fuzzy sphere that gives the O(2) Wilson-Fisher theory at a quantum critical point. The fuzzy-sphere setup keeps full spin symmetry, so energy states line up one-to-one with theory operators. With exact diagonalization and matrix product states plus perturbation theory, they find 48 primary operators and their descendants. The lowest primary scaling dimensions match bootstrap predictions well.
arxiv-2604-18805: Ríos-García and seven colleagues evaluate language model based scientific agents across eight domains through more than 25,000 agent runs, asking whether their reasoning follows the norms that make science self correcting. The base model, not the agent scaffold, drives performance and behavior. Evidence is ignored in 68 percent of traces, while refutation driven belief revision occurs in only 26 percent, and convergent multi test evidence is scarce. The same pattern persists even with near complete successful reasoning trajectories as context, so outcome based evaluation cannot detect these failures.
arxiv-2604-18905: Li, Duong, and Zanotto present a task adaptive admittance controller for human quadrotor cooperative load transport. Earlier physical human robot work focused on manipulator arms, while human quadrotor load transport remains new. Their quadrotor carries an actively controlled winch, and the controller adapts the cable to contact forces during transport. Tests covered loading, unloading, and transport with variable and fixed cable lengths under low and high stiffness. The new method beats the conventional approach in responsiveness and motion smoothness.
arxiv-2604-19105: Hou and seven colleagues study first-person motion generation from views and language instructions. They spot a reasoning-generation tangle: joint reasoning and motion training creates gradient clashes harming grounding and motion quality. Like the split between thinking and motor control, EgoMotion works in two stages. In Cognitive Reasoning, a vision-language model maps inputs into discrete motion codes, building goal-consistent plans bridging perception and action. In Motion Generation, these codes drive a diffusion motion generator.
arxiv-2604-19205: Tam, Colpaert, and Taelman present online schema alignment for Link Traversal Query Processing, finding, scoping, and applying rules during execution while keeping behavior. Decentralized knowledge graph querying merges data without a center but suffers from vocabulary heterogeneity, which issuers cannot fully anticipate, especially for local, scoped, or runtime rules. The demo tests it on a social case via a Comunica interface. Source, a CLI tool, and a library are public. Online schema alignment recovers complete results with low overhead, a base for web reasoning.
arxiv-2604-19405: Laskar and colleagues introduce MM-JudgeBench, a first large-scale test for judge models across languages and modalities. Auto judges like reward models matter for aligning large vision-language models, yet they are almost always tested in English only. The test holds over 60,000 pairwise preference cases spanning 25 diverse languages. It pairs a general vision-language subset with a chart-centric reasoning subset.
arxiv-2604-19605: Shin tests how global assets align with United States put-call parity residuals. Put-call parity is risk-neutral at terminal payoff, but enforcement is path-dependent and capital-using. The author tests whether the SPX and RUT carry gap is explained by OIS-based funding, volatility, trading friction, and financial conditions, or by outside information. Adding IEFA, IGOV, and IAU improves in-sample and leave-one-year-out fit after United States-centered controls. Gains survive broad-dollar neutralization and robustness checks, supporting reduced-form P-Q alignment.
arxiv-2604-19905: Feng and five colleagues built ViBR, a tool that replays software bugs straight from screen-capture videos. Such videos are a popular bug-report format, but hard to replay by machine. ViBR cuts actions apart with CLIP embedding similarity, then checks interface states and guides replay with vision-language models. It reproduced 72 percent of test recordings, well ahead of leading baselines and ablated variants.
arxiv-2604-20105: Lee and five colleagues present EnergAIzer, a fast, accurate tool for estimating GPU power for AI workloads. Existing models stall not on modeling but on getting hardware use inputs, via costly simulation or profiling. EnergAIzer predicts those inputs with a lightweight model built from structured kernel patterns, cutting walltime from hours to seconds. It reaches 8 percent power error on NVIDIA Ampere GPUs and predicts H100 power with just 7 percent error, for power-aware design studies.
arxiv-2604-20805: LaCroix argues that the value alignment problem for AI is better seen as a structural question about governance. The real question is how much alignment, for whom, and at what price. He borrows the principal-agent framework from economics, tracing misalignment to three linked axes: objectives, information, and principals. It clarifies that alignment is not a single tech trait but an outcome shaped by aims, information, and stakes. It must be managed through formal steps that set aims, check systems, and let groups contest calls.
arxiv-2604-20905: Caputo and Buonocore propose a problem-based way to teach probability, drawing on the Data and Predictions strand of the Indicazioni Nazionali per il curricolo 2012. The study uses design-based research in a single cycle of two teaching rounds in the same class across two back-to-back years. Within this frame, a set of hand-picked problems is used to spark student engagement. These problems are made not only to bring in probabilistic concepts, but also to spur students' talk and argument skills.
arxiv-2604-21005: Dastider and co-authors build a chaos test tool for ion-molecule reactions in cold planetary atmospheres. There, proton-transfer chains shape what the air is made of. They combine multireference electronic structure, adiabatic gauge potentials, and random matrix theory. Their test cases are H3+ and H5+ systems, the kind found around Jupiter. The transition state acts as a choke point where chaos is notably damped, boosting tunneling. A fragility index from the gauge slope gauges how mode motion restores chaos and cuts the rate.
arxiv-2604-21105: Dolz, Kolton, and Fasano simulate tiny vortex crystals forming inside micron-sized superconductors as they cool. Their calculations show defects near the sample edges heal in step with measurements on a bismuth-based material. The defect pattern freezes below the melting point, shaped by both vortex structure and confinement. The findings extend to other confined soft materials whose tiny crystals must form in tight spaces.
arxiv-2604-21205: Linxiu Zeng, Emily Kuang, and Jian Zhao study how presenters handle constraints while building slide decks for stories that keep changing. A study of ten presenters yields the CMPA framework, treating time, audience, and communicative intent as shaping forces rather than mere limits. Their ReSlide prototype turns constraints into active design drivers, and two user studies show it helps presenters reuse and adapt material across sessions as constraints evolve.
arxiv-2604-21905: Li, Zhang, and Giannakis revisit low-rank adaptation, the standard for low-cost fine-tuning of foundation models, through signal processing. LoRA enables adaptation of billion-weight networks with minimal overhead, yet which design choices, tuning tricks, and deployment limits should guide method selection remains unclear. The overview bridges modern adapter designs with classical low-rank tools and inverse problems, stressing mechanisms over lists or comparisons. Advances fall into design, tuning, and uses, from SVD factorisation and rank growth to starting points, solvers, and gauge-safe tuning.
arxiv-2604-22105: Sharma and thirteen colleagues use fast radio bursts to probe cosmic-web baryons via dispersion measures encoding electron density along sightlines. From 3,455 CHIME/FRB sources with roughly 15 arcmin spots, they map dispersion links with structure and baryon tracers to redshift under 2. They find significant links at 2.6 to 5 sigma with ten probes, including galaxies and lensing. Also covered: CMB lensing, Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, X-ray emission, soft X-ray background, and radio continuum. Overdense sightlines carry larger dispersion measures, and hot-gas links gauge feedback strength.
arxiv-2604-22205: Chun and five colleagues study how pre-service teachers can practice running classroom argumentation. A formative study with eight veteran teachers sets needs: tailoring, lifelike simulations, reflection, and ease of use. Building on these, they develop ArguMath, an AI-mock classroom with three parts. They are classroom setup; talk simulation with AI students from real transcripts and real-time tips; and review through discourse notes and feedback. A trial study with seven pre-service teachers and four veteran talks shows ArguMath can support orchestration skills, particularly theory-aligned questioning.
arxiv-2604-22505: Ke, Qin, and Zhang tackle private database lookup under hostile servers. Private retrieval hides which entry a client wants, yet a malicious server can still corrupt the answer. Earlier authenticated schemes resist selective-failure tricks but lean on computational hardness. Verified information-theoretic schemes give integrity without such assumptions, yet offer only weak query privacy and no selective-failure defense. The authors define unconditionally secure authenticated retrieval rigorously, place the verified variant beneath it as a relaxed cousin, and prove valid verified schemes upgrade directly with no extra overhead.
arxiv-2604-22605: Myers and eight colleagues study how mass loss and overshooting shape the core and glow of red supergiants. Before collapse, neutrino output from a red supergiant would become visible in neutrino detectors. Emission rates and spectra depend on core temperature, density, and composition, which shift in the last year as burning speeds up and deleptonization begins. Stellar model uncertainties, including mass loss and such treatments, alter core state and makeup near collapse, and thus pre-collapse output. The study varies the treatments, tracking effects on core traits and neutrino output.
arxiv-2604-22705: Waite closes an investigation into periodic colorings of locally finite graphs, asking when a coloring repeats under only finitely many symmetry orbits. For planar graphs with a single end, he proves a periodic proper vertex coloring always exists, built from maps into the Euclidean and hyperbolic planes that respect isometries. In the Euclidean case, five colors always suffice.
arxiv-2604-22905: Wu and six colleagues propose CT-guided, spatially varying regularization for deformable whole-body PET registration, the alignment of scans used to characterize tumors and track metastatic disease. Standard methods use one global weight to steady the displacement field, but rigid bones need stronger regularization than soft tissues. Their method builds a voxel-wise regularization map from the paired CT volume, adapting strength across anatomy. On a clinical data set of 296 patients, it significantly improves whole-body and organ-wise alignment over a weakly supervised baseline.
arxiv-2604-23005: Lawrence, Wang, and Segal tune environmental noise itself to enhance quantum transport, instead of tuning system settings under uniform noise. In one-dimensional lattices with ramped or disordered energy landscapes, they apply site-dependent dephasing within a Lindblad framework to raise steady-state flux. For ramp potentials, short-range tunneling favors dephasing on alternating sites, while long-range tunneling favors a profile rising with distance from the source. In all cases site-tuned dephasing beats uniform dephasing in efficiency, with greater spatial delocalization of the steady state.
arxiv-2604-23305: Moerman and nine colleagues present gateau, a modular open-source simulator for submillimeter IFU observations with kinetic inductance detectors. A Python interface over a C/C++ CUDA backend sends source signals through atmospheric screens, scan patterns, and telescope settings to the detectors. Photon noise enters as white noise on received power, detector noise as correlated pink noise, with outputs stored as time-ordered sets. Checked against DESHIMA 2.0 views of the atmosphere and Uranus, gateau simulates long observations in far less time than the observations themselves.
arxiv-2604-23405: Baker, Van Benschoten, and Shepherd extend structure factor twist averaging, a low-cost method reproducing twist-averaged CCSD energies, to low-dimensional materials. Two variants, paired sfTA and binding sfTA, change which twist angles enter the protocol and how the special angle is chosen, using the binding structure factor. Both variants are tested on bilayer systems against original sfTA, with binding sfTA giving the most accurate energies approaching twist-averaged results. Contour plots suggest the gains come mostly from cancellation of errors.
arxiv-2604-23605: Lv and six colleagues build DxChain, a clinical reasoning system that mirrors how doctors think instead of jumping straight to a diagnosis. It first builds a full patient baseline to avoid cold-start hallucinations, then plans ahead with a medical tree-of-thoughts search, and finally settles evidence conflicts through adversarial Angel-Devil debates. On two real clinical benchmarks it sets a new mark for diagnostic accuracy and logical consistency.
arxiv-2604-23705: Mijoski and Karbevski ask whether a plain multilayer perceptron of the same width can exactly absorb its own skip connection, computing the same function without the residual path. No such absorption exists at any depth or for any activation in today's frontier language models. For plain ReLU and GELU, absorption is possible only on a measure-zero set of weights, so the two families are generically disjoint.
arxiv-2604-23805: Borysov and colleagues report the first performance of the E320 tracker, a scaled-down detector for measuring single positrons from electron-laser collisions at SLAC's FACET-II facility. Five layers of single-chip sensors, installed in 2024, track positrons from photon conversion as a proxy for the nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process. Even under extreme background hit density, the measured signal rate matches the expected Breit-Wheeler rate, with false positives far smaller.
arxiv-2604-24005: Wang and four colleagues tackle unstable training when small models learn multi-turn agent skills from teachers. As student errors pile up across turns, the student drifts past what the teacher can supervise, so divergence climbs while success falls. Their TCOD curriculum exposes only short trajectories at first and lengthens them gradually, steadying training and lifting agent scores by up to 18 points across three benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-24105: Goda, Liu, and Tempone propose a new randomized digital net design whose generating matrices are Hankel matrices picked at random. Compared with earlier designs, the approach simplifies construction and needs fewer random variables while keeping good convergence rates with fitting estimators. The paper analyzes the design, bounds Walsh coefficients, and gives error analysis for a median-of-means estimator and a new greedy selection rule. That rule picks the best design from a batch by worst-case error. Numerical experiments confirm the theory and show strong practical performance.
arxiv-2604-24305: Panda, Mohapatra, and Mohanta study heavy neutral leptons in B decays as probes beyond the Standard Model. Focusing on leptonic channels, they constrain the mass and mixing plane with data. They then examine lepton-number-violating processes from on-shell heavy neutral leptons, including two-muon B decays. At mixing of one part in a million and masses of 2 to 3 gigaelectronvolts, branching ratios reach one part in a hundred million. The B_c channel shows the largest enhancement; the J/psi channel is suppressed.
arxiv-2604-24405: Zhou and three colleagues study how user traits shape browsing of diverse movie picks in an LLM multi-agent system. A study with 100 users tests a single-agent system against a multi-agent movie system. The multi-agent system clearly raises felt novelty and Shannon diversity. Conscientiousness tracks with felt scores and diversity, while extraversion tracks against felt diversity. GenAI past use tracks with Shannon diversity, while GenAI doubt tracks against it. System design also mixes with user traits, warning against one-size-fits-all multi-agent designs.
arxiv-2604-24905: Bańka and Chudziak propose MultiHedge for adaptive control. It uses retrieval-based control under changing settings. Old approaches fail across shifting regimes and behave unstably. MultiHedge has a language model decide allocations from past cases. Execution follows standard option strategies. In U.S. equities tests, it beats rule and learning baselines. Memory-based retrieval beats model scale alone for robustness and stability. Memory and design drive robustness in modular systems.
arxiv-2604-25005: Greenlees maps the spectral space of subgroup classes of Sp(2). It is a union, disjoint, of finitely many blocks, each led by a subgroup. 26 blocks have dimension 1, 6 have dimension 2, and the rest are single points. Each block carries a sheaf of poly rings and components. These parts build an abelian category designed to reflect rational Sp(2)-equivariant cohomology theories. Assembling results, he shows rational Sp(2)-spectra form a category Quillen equivalent to differential graded objects of that category.
arxiv-2604-25105: Ghosh and four colleagues report clear energy transfer signals in action spectra of a cyanobacterial protein. Yet excited-state energy and charge transfer signals have been absent in typical proteins. That suggested limits for probing large aggregates. The authors measure energy transfer in this protein via conventional and fluorescence methods, finding fluorescence signals strong and comparable to conventional ones. Experiment and simulations suggest the size limit changes for cyanobacterial proteins because of slow annihilation.
arxiv-2604-25705: Jin, Ye, and Ma propose a direct way to characterize classical noise that makes a qubit lose phase coherence, using repeated Ramsey interferometry measurements. Compared with filter-function spectroscopy, their method uses simpler pulse control. It is less limited by probe coherence time, and can detect correlation functions of any order in slowly varying noise. Each short measurement samples the noise field directly, so correlations among measurement outcomes mirror correlations of the noise itself. Numerical tests on Gaussian and two-level fluctuator noise support the approach.
arxiv-2604-25805: Zhou offers a minimal theory for polar pairing at amorphous LaAlO3/KTaO3 interfaces. There, superconductivity coexists with switchable polar regions, and critical temperature tracks orientation in a near-linear way. Overdamped polar fluctuations mediate pairing. Geometric Rashba coupling sets its angular pattern, with the leading vertex scaling as sine of the angle to the crystal axis. Numerical work reproduces that curve. Strong tantalum coupling explains sharper orientation sensitivity than SrTiO3.
arxiv-2604-25905: Potts and Sudhof study how user skill with AI shapes what AI delivers, using 27,000 annotated transcripts from WildChat. Fluent users take on harder tasks and iterate collaboratively, refining goals and judging outputs critically, while novices stay passive. That gap yields a paradox: fluent users fail more often, but their failures are visible, more likely to partly recover, and paired with greater success on complex tasks. Novices more often suffer invisible failures, where chats look successful but miss the mark.
arxiv-2604-26005: Boccia and Chianese study asteroid-mass primordial black holes as dark matter in supersymmetry. Heavy minimal-supersymmetric particles can transiently soften the early equation of state. That softening during the transition boosts black hole formation. For masses above about 10^5 GeV, the mass function rises sharply in the asteroid-mass window. That lets black holes supply all dark matter within bounds. Standard Model versions of the same setups give mass functions observations exclude. Lighter spectra shift production above about 10^22 grams, where microlensing limits cut their share.
arxiv-2604-26505: Foerster and five colleagues exposed a privacy leak in dynamic quantization, where run-time scaling adapts to each batch's data. An adversary sharing a batch can exploit that adaptation as a side channel, recovering part or all of a fellow user's batched input. The team found at least four popular frameworks default to, or allow, configurations that leak across batch boundaries. They named the phenomenon Quantamination, warning that serving efficiency gains can carry serious cross-user exposure.
arxiv-2604-26705: Lei, Qiao, Zepf, Xia, and Welsh present a theory of relativistic surface plasmon excitation at a smooth plasma interface driven by a laser pulse. From Maxwell's equations and a cold plasma response, they derive and solve a driven wave equation. An infinite planar surface conserves the in-plane wave number. Interaction length or axial modulation supplies an axial spectrum. Cylindrical curvature swaps a continuous wave number with an azimuthal mode index. Surface geometry controls the effect, and curved surfaces can sustain an on-axis field that speeds particles.
arxiv-2604-26805: Liu and twelve colleagues present Bian Que, a system for operating online search and advertising services. It sorts work into release checks, routine inspection, and alert tracing, giving each task a skill naming its data and rules. Agents can generate those skills, engineers refine them in plain words, and corrections improve stored knowledge and the skills. On Kuaishou's search engine it cut alert volume by 75 percent and fix time by more than half.
arxiv-2604-27105: Kosmydel, Gajewski and Białek propose a dual-stream Transformer detecting mutual gaze and joint attention from synchronized dual-camera recordings. Manual coding here is slow work, and multi-camera dynamics are hard to compute. Their approach uses frozen gaze-aware backbones for visual priors, with custom token fusion mapping spatial and semantic relations between pairs. On caregiver-infant interactions, the model beats a convolutional baseline and a top multimodal large language model. The authors share model and weights as a scalable tool for behavioral scientists, tunable to diverse labs.
arxiv-2604-27405: Cacioli adapts the Reliable Change Index from clinical psychology to compare Llama and Qwen versions item by item on 2,000 MMLU-Pro questions. Most items show no reliable change in either pair, yet analysable items move both ways, with gains partly cancelled by losses. Low-accuracy items tend to improve while high-accuracy items worsen, and Llama loses physics while Qwen loses law. Greedy single-shot evaluation misses 42 percent of changed items and falsely flags 25 percent of unchanged ones, so he recommends reporting churn with aggregate accuracy.
arxiv-2604-27705: Simoes and Colombo study robust control of a catenary robot: two quadrotors joined by a fixed cable. The cable acts as a geometric part shaped by the drone setup, and its shape sets forces coupling the vehicles' motion. They propose a geometric tracking control for the agents' relative setup and analyze toughness to messy doubt in cable-induced forces. The main result gives local input-to-state stability of closed-loop tracking errors, with convergence in the nominal case and a clear final bound under bounded force shifts.
arxiv-2604-27805: Chishti, Oyinloye, and Li address cross-chain NFT moves of online assets with functions and pledges between blockchains. Design gaps create fit hurdles, as base tools move data but cannot resolve deeper issues in state, transaction, and ownership records. They derive a tailored four-layer NFT stack splitting crypto, state, transaction, and ownership parts, and define good moves as feature keeping. Their four-phase method sorts each feature as preserved, partly mismatched, or fully mismatched, and an Ethereum-to-Solana trial finds several mismatch issues.
arxiv-2604-28105: Roy and colleagues report evidence that moderate cobalt doping turns the narrow-gap semiconductor FeSb2 into a metallic altermagnet that survives to room temperature. Infrared conductivity shows low-energy transitions that appear with doping and grow as cobalt rises, and theory traces them solely to altermagnetic spin order. Doping also mixes infrared phonon modes while leaving spin symmetry intact, making carrier-tuned FeSb2 a platform for metallic d-wave altermagnetism.
arxiv-2605-00005:
Pragya Sharma, Hang Qiu, and Mani Srivastava revisit a settled assumption in distributed real-time computing: that inference must run on the device. Cyber-physical systems use deep neural networks for perception, but local hardware pays heavy energy and computing costs to meet control deadlines. Cloud inference was long dismissed because network delays vary too much for safety-critical loops.

The authors build a formal model of distributed inference latency from sensing frequency, platform throughput, network delay, and task safety limits. They test it on emergency braking for autonomous driving, with simulations using real-time vehicle dynamics. With strong cloud hardware, network and queueing delays are amortized, and the cloud matches or beats on-device inference, holding safety margins more reliably under the conditions they identify.
arxiv-2605-00105:
M Fogliardi and eight co-authors use convolutional networks to read the structure of galaxy clusters from weak lensing maps. Clusters are the most massive bound structures in the universe and key probes of cosmic evolution, but coming surveys will deliver too many for hand analysis. Their networks infer structural parameters from the subtle distortions that a cluster's gravity imprints on background galaxies.

Three architectures are trained on tens of thousands of synthetic shear maps of simulated clusters. Together they predict five parameters at once: virial mass, concentration, substructure count, and the smooth mass fraction among them. On thousands of test clusters, mass estimates stay robust under realistic noise and concentrations are stable, while substructure counts are systematically underestimated. Against traditional profile fitting, the best network is nearly unbiased in mass with fewer systematic errors, offering a scalable route for large surveys.
arxiv-2605-00305:
Tianqi Shi and Jinxin Xue take on Aubry's completeness conjecture, a claim about twist maps and the physics of atomic chains. In the Frenkel-Kontorova model of atoms on a surface, whether the chain conducts or insulates hinges on how rotation numbers vary with a stiffness-like parameter. Aubry predicted that this variation forms a complete devil's staircase, a curve that climbs only in jumps.

The authors present an argument for the conjecture when all minimal configurations are uniformly hyperbolic, the strongly chaotic case. In that regime they argue the rotation number graph is purely singularly continuous, matching Aubry's picture. They also argue the opposite case: when a positive share of orderly KAM tori survives, the staircase is incomplete. The phenomenon is kin to phase locking in circle maps and to steps in the fractional quantum Hall effect.
arxiv-2605-00405:
Kang Yang and 4 co-authors tackle cooperative perception for vehicles and robots whose detectors were trained separately, by different developers, with no joint preparation. In the wild, such agents meet only occasionally and online. Simply fusing their features, the authors find, performs worse than one agent perceiving alone, because the feature languages do not match.

Their module, BOLT, adapts neighbors' features on the fly using the host agent as teacher, needing no ground-truth labels. Confident host features guide the alignment, while neighbors are invited to fill the regions where the host is unsure. The module is tiny by modern standards and plugs into existing systems. On two driving benchmarks it lifted detection scores far above unadapted fusion and consistently beat working alone, across pairing and fusion choices.
arxiv-2605-00505:
Lu Dai and 6 co-authors argue that information retrieval must be rebuilt for its new main reader: the language model. Search feeds chatbots and agents that answer with outside sources, and models can only take in so much at once and have a weakness for noise. Off-topic or false text is no longer a nuisance; it leads to invented answers and broken reasoning.

The authors frame the shift as denoising, raising the density of usable, checked evidence inside a model's window. They sort the field's challenges into four stages: information that cannot be reached, that is hard to find, that is mismatched, and that cannot be checked. A sorting then groups noise-cutting methods across indexing, search, context handling, and checks in agent workflows. The paper closes with denoising work in search-heavy domains such as personal helpers, coding agents, deep research tools, and image-and-text systems.
arxiv-2605-00705:
Martin Bendersky, Salvatore Elia, and Jelena Grbic study the shape and holes of Vietoris-Rips complexes built from hypercube graphs. These complexes turn a graph into a higher-dimensional object whose cohomology, a tool for counting holes, can reveal hidden structure. The authors build a framework that connects the complexes to rings and related objects from algebra.

Their methods yield lower bounds on how connected the complexes must be and the first global upper bounds on a related property. The bounds produce endless families that contradict Shukla's conjecture. They also build explicit cohomology classes from simpler ones and introduce ghost vertices, a new tool for finding and separating such classes.
arxiv-2605-00905:
Anirudh Iyengar Kaniyar Narayana Iyengar and six co-authors present DIAGRAMS, a review framework for reasoning-level attribution in diagram question answering. Answering questions about diagrams, charts, maps, circuits, and infographics requires linking each answer to all visual regions used in the reasoning, not just the region holding the final answer. Building such evidence is slow, and tools often tie their interface to one dataset format.

DIAGRAMS decouples the interface from dataset structures through an internal meta-schema and adapters. Given an image and question, it proposes the regions needed for reasoning, can generate missing questions or regions, and supports human checking and refinement. Across six datasets, suggested evidence agrees strongly with reviewer-final selections.
arxiv-2605-01005:
Tiger Lu and Garett Brown implement coordinates suited to wide binary systems in TRACE, a hybrid integrator inside the widely used REBOUND N-body package. Traditional hybrid integrators perform poorly in this regime, where two bodies orbit far apart while close encounters can still occur between any pair. The new coordinate system supports such encounters across the whole system.

Benchmarks cover planet-planet scattering, stellar flybys, and ZLK oscillations. In wide binary coordinates, TRACE stays qualitatively correct in cases where other hybrid methods fail. In many cases its results are statistically similar to the high-precision IAS15 integrator, with speedups up to about nine times. The authors also give guidelines for when use of these coordinates is appropriate.
arxiv-2605-01105:
Xinfeng Xu and fourteen co-authors develop methods for fitting multi-phase galactic wind models to high-quality outflow observations. Galactic winds shape galaxy evolution, but outflowing gas spans several ionization phases and varies spatially, making model fitting hard. They fit column density profiles using a multiphase, multiscale wind model, identifying three key parameters: initial hot and cool phase mass-loading factors and initial cool-cloud mass.

Good fits are obtained for most galaxies, with tight constraints on the cool-phase loading and moderate constraints on the other parameters. Inferred loadings are mostly of order unity with significant scatter. Interaction between phases lets cool-outflow observations indirectly constrain the hot wind. Predicted trends include cool outflow velocity rising then plateauing with radius.
arxiv-2605-01205:
Quoc Phong Dao and six co-authors introduce Span Representation Alignment for distilling large language models across different tokenizers. Cross-tokenizer distillation transfers knowledge to a smaller student even when they differ, but existing token-level alignment is brittle and sensitive to tokenizer gaps. The authors argue how tokens are grouped into robust views before distillation matters just as much as the matching itself.

Their framework shifts the unit from tokens to tokenizer-free spans, modeled through a physical multi-particle lens. Each span's state is an attention-weighted center of mass that captures semantic information, with salient spans prioritized. A geometric regularizer preserves span structure, and aligned span logit teaching enhances transfer. Cross-architecture experiments show consistent, significant gains over leading baselines.
arxiv-2605-01305:
Himanshu Kumar Dwivedi, Matthias Ehrhardt, and Rajeev combine neural networks with a high-order time scheme to solve fractional equations, a class where the present state depends on the whole past. Such equations often have a sharp kink at the start, which ruins accuracy on even time grids.

Their design, Alikhanov-XfPINNs, pairs the Alikhanov scheme on stretched time grids with a physics-informed network that learns the solution. A flexible activation function speeds training, and the loss is built from the scheme itself, with start and edge rules set as hard or soft limits. A separate time-stepping setup lets them check time errors apart from training errors. Tests on cases with known and unknown exact answers show robust results and large savings in computing time.
arxiv-2605-01405:
Oliver Eggenberger Andersen and four co-authors ask how often a collapsing star forms a black hole partway through its own explosion. In this outcome, called a black hole supernova, the shock revives and the blast starts, but a black hole forms before the explosion finishes.

The team runs 23 long two-dimensional simulations of stars from about 20 to 60 times the Sun's mass, spanning a range of core tightness. Eighteen runs end as black hole supernovae, spread across nearly the whole mass range, with the hole forming between well under a second and a few seconds after core bounce. Final blast energies and hole masses vary widely, and hole mass tracks the carbon-oxygen core mass, though that core alone mispredicts both ends of the range. A three-dimensional check shows how geometry changes the picture.
arxiv-2605-01605:
Zhuoyun Li and eight co-authors locate exactly where a small prompt typo breaks a language model's answer. Robustness work usually grades the whole response, which can hide a drift that hits one key entity, relation, or conclusion while the rest reads fine.

Their framework works at segment level. Clean and perturbed answers are cut into meaning segments, aligned by an optimal-transport objective, and the worst-drifting segments are penalized. An adapter-stability term, guided by how attention reallocates across segments, keeps the low-rank tuning from amplifying those shifts; a PAC-Bayesian view explains why capping adapter growth should transfer to unseen noise. On summarization tests the method hardens models against typos, deletions, synonym swaps, and paraphrases, keeps clean scores competitive, and transfers across data sets better than whole-sequence rivals.
arxiv-2605-01805:
Yu and four colleagues design a learning signal that helps teams of AI agents coordinate. In multi-agent reinforcement learning, several agents learn together toward a shared goal, but each one only sees its own view of the world. A helpful move may pay off for a teammate later, yet the shared team reward gives no direct credit for it. Their framework, MAGIC, estimates how one agent's action shapes its teammates' futures over several steps, then turns only the beneficial effects into extra rewards.

Counterfactual comparisons pit what actually happened against what would have happened under a different action, and an advantage gate steers exploration toward moves aligned with the task. On particle-world tasks and StarCraft micromanagement benchmarks, MAGIC beat leading prior methods, with average relative gains of about twenty-seven percent and ten percent. The result suggests that crediting cross-agent influence step by step builds steadier teamwork.
arxiv-2605-02105:
Ishaan Watts and colleagues show that how a model is pretrained affects how much it forgets during later training and quantisation. Optimisers are usually tuned for the strongest base model, assuming strength alone carries through later changes. The authors argue the shape of the base model, in particular how flat its minimum is, controls what survives updates.

They test three ways to bias training toward flat minima: sharpness-aware minimisation, large learning rates, and shorter rate annealing. Across model sizes and five data sets, all three cut forgetting, by up to eighty percent. At larger scale, a short sharpness-aware phase on an existing one-billion-parameter checkpoint cut forgetting after maths training and after four-bit quantisation.
arxiv-2605-02205:
Mahdi Nouraie, Houying Zhu, and Samuel Muller improve stability selection, a method that picks features by how often they survive resampling. Standard stability selection resamples rows but leaves the design fixed. An irrelevant feature that correlates with relevant ones can then be picked often, breaking the condition behind the false-positive bound.

Their 2D method also varies the design, by adding a grid of injected noise to the inputs and aggregating selection counts over both half-samples and noise levels. At zero noise it reduces to the original method. Input noise acts like a ridge penalty on average, so a jittered Lasso fit can repair some broken designs, though it can also hurt. The paper gives the noise level where a violated feature's statistic vanishes in one case.
arxiv-2605-02405:
Sofianos Panagiotis Fotias and Vassilis Gaganis build closed-loop controllers for carbon storage in rock. Injection and brine output must adapt as the reservoir responds in uncertain ways. Only data that are truly available during operation can be used. The authors cast the task as a decision problem with partial views. They train deep learning controllers in high-fidelity reservoir models.

They compare several policy types, from full-state and well-only designs to history-based and teacher-student variants. That comparison shows the value of past well responses. It also shows the value of full simulator states during training. A latent model pipeline then reuses learned dynamics and retunes controllers under injector failure, leakage, and changed reservoir links. History-based policies recovered nearly all full-state performance.
arxiv-2605-02505:
Sangpil Youm, Leah Jones, and Bonnie J. Dorr revisit semantic role labeling, the task of marking who did what to whom in a sentence. Large language models handle meaning in a hidden way, with few clear structural checks. Older role-labeling tools also face a practical problem: a once-standard framework entered maintenance mode in late 2022, limiting its fit with new encoders.

The authors offer a modern encoder-based system that keeps explicit predicate and argument structure while running inference about ten times faster. Stronger encoders lift accuracy within the same design. A diagnostic method informed by dependency grammar traces span errors and probes how language models react to structural signals. The main gain from those cues, they find, is stability of structure.
arxiv-2605-03305:
Ankit Kumar, Daniel A. Caballero, Hajime Sotani, and Nicolás Yunes develop the first fully relativistic treatment of non-radial oscillations in two-fluid neutron stars whose fluids couple only through gravity. Such oscillations probe star structure and gravity, but prior work lacked a complete relativistic setup for independently conserved currents.

They derive the coupled perturbation equations for the metric and both fluids, with the regularity, surface, and matching conditions needed for a well-posed mode problem. Numerical spectra follow for sample stars, and mode branches are classed by whether the inner or outer fluid dominates, laying groundwork for gravitational wave studies.
arxiv-2605-03405:
Alexander Matyasko, Xin Lou, Indriyati Atmosukarto, and Wei Zhang introduce TsallisPGD, an adversarial attack on semantic segmentation models. Flipping thousands of pixel labels at once is far harder than fooling a classifier, and standard cross-entropy wastes effort on pixels already fooled, overstating robustness.

Their attack uses Tsallis cross-entropy, whose parameter steers gradient focus across pixel confidence levels. No single fixed value wins everywhere, so a dynamic schedule sweeps it during optimization. On three datasets, one validation-chosen schedule gave the best average rank against five rival attacks, on both standard and robust models.
arxiv-2605-03705:
Philipp Czerner, Javier Esparza, and Konrad Winslow present iSMC, a model checker that certifies its own answers through dialogue. Model checking verifies whether a system satisfies a logical property. iSMC handles arbitrary Computation Tree Logic properties with justice requirements. It uses symbolic binary decision diagrams. After solving an instance, it runs a certification step.

The certification rests on interactive proof systems. A dialogue guarantees, with a user-chosen high probability, that the reported answer is correct. iSMC adapts technology from a certified QBF solver presented at CAV 2023, reshaped for CTL model checking. The authors describe it as the first self-certifying model checker of its kind.
arxiv-2605-04505:
Leying Zhang and four co-authors present a framework for judging the quality of generated audio and speech, an area where evaluation methods have lagged behind the fast-improving generators. Standard metrics and general multimodal models often fail to generalise, handle new tasks without retraining, or follow flexible instructions.

Their system connects a frozen high-performance audio encoder to a fine-tuned language model through a trainable adapter, and frames assessment as an instruction-following reasoning task. A broad data pipeline varies sources, tasks, calibrations, and descriptions to build robustness. Across speech, sound, music, and unseen domains, its scores tracked human ratings more closely than rival general models.
arxiv-2605-04705:
Jiangnan Zhu and three co-authors propose a watermarking scheme for 3D medical scans. It protects their ownership and authenticity when they are shared for telemedicine. Such volume data are valuable for diagnosis but easy to copy or tamper with once they travel across networks.

Their method is reversible and leaves the host data untouched. It is a zero-watermarking design. A feature extractor trained with contrastive learning pulls stable, distinctive features from each volume. They are robust to 3D attacks. Watermark bits are embedded by expanding differences between neighbouring voxels. The voxels sit inside small cubes of a wavelet transform. A majority vote during extraction improves reliability, while keeping distortion low.
arxiv-2605-04905:
Mehrab Mahdian, Ferenc Ender, and Tamas Pardy ask whether machine learning models agree on which settings matter most in electrospinning, a sensitive way to make fine fibres. Small changes in operating conditions can alter fibre shape and performance, and many studies trust a single model's ranking of those conditions. That trust may be misplaced, the authors argue.

They trained twenty-one models of many types on ninety-six experiments with polyvinyl alcohol and compared rankings using SHAP values. Models with similar accuracy often ranked features quite differently, showing prediction and explanation are separate qualities. Solution concentration stood out as the most consistent influence across model families.
arxiv-2605-05105:
Gerald Ogbonna, David Bindel, and Lindsay Anderson tackle reducing harmful transients in electric power networks by reshaping the network itself. Reliable operation grows harder as variable renewable generation joins the grid. Their setup uses graph Laplacian matrices, which encode how buses in the network connect, and shows the design problem is convex under stated assumptions.

A matrix condition ensures that steady-state phase angles exist, are unique, and hold together, and it can be added directly as a constraint. On the standard IEEE thirty-bus test system, the method picked out critical links, and dynamic runs showed much smaller transients and better performance measures. A reweighting shortcut explores the trade-off between sparsity and optimality.
arxiv-2605-05405:
James Walsh and four co-authors built GeoQuery, a way to search satellite imagery using plain language. Archives of Earth photos are huge, but picture-based search models cannot understand text queries. Training a joint model needs paired data and computing power that are not available at global scale.

GeoQuery avoids that training with a two-stage trick. It writes text descriptions for a subset of one hundred thousand map tiles, tuned so text distances mirror visual distances. Queries search the text first, then the wider visual archive. On disaster queries it placed floods best, and responders used it during a Brisbane cyclone.
arxiv-2605-05505:
Superconducting radio-frequency cavities need coatings that survive curved shapes. Aaron Gobeyn, Wolfgang Ackermann, and Herbert De Gersem model what uneven coating does to a cavity's quality factor. Their multilayer coatings stack superconductor, insulator, and superconductor, allowing brittle materials that bulk niobium cannot offer.

They generate the thickness unevenness with Gaussian random fields at eight length scales, with over two thousand samples each. Quality factors came out normally distributed, with spread growing as the length scale grew. Mean values barely moved, though in extreme cases the quality factor shifted by a few percent.
arxiv-2605-05705:
Computing integrals with kernel quadrature can beat random sampling, but its tuned weights often go negative and unstable. Satoshi Hayakawa asks whether the speed survives when weights are forced positive. In his setting, a pool of already-scored candidate points must be reweighted to approach a kernel mean.

He shows the problem is governed by the random convex hull the pool generates, not by its plain average. The geometry yields error bounds for positive-weight rules, showing exactly which quantity controls the error. The results clarify when simplex weights keep spectral acceleration and when forcing positive weights costs real accuracy.
arxiv-2605-05905:
Daniel Cortild and Coralia Cartis introduce a new way to add privacy to machine learning training. Objective perturbation protects data by adding random terms to the training goal. The linear version needs bounded gradients, a strong assumption that rules out many modern models.

Their quadratic version instead adds a random quadratic form to the goal. That change creates strong convexity and stability through curvature, so privacy rests on spectral traits of the added term, not on gradient bounds. They prove privacy holds even when the problem is solved only in part. They also give utility bounds on excess risk, compare the method with the linear version, and show modern splitting methods can solve the resulting problems well.
arxiv-2605-06005:
Sarka Liskova and five co-authors build a sign language recognition system that runs on neuromorphic hardware. Recent recognizers are accurate, but their delay and power needs block real time use on small devices. Neuromorphic chips compute with sparse spikes, which suits fast, low power perception at the edge.

Their system pairs a spiking visual attention step, which picks out the region of interest online, with a compact spiking network on the SpiNNaker platform. It targets American Sign Language fingerspelling and was tested on two event based data sets. Accuracy reached 92.27 percent in simulation and 83.1 percent on the hardware itself. The design used just 0.565 milliwatts with a three millisecond delay, the leanest figures among the compared approaches.
arxiv-2605-06305:
Thomas Cory and Axel Küpper use language models to label personal data leaking through web and mobile app traffic. Privacy audits scan outbound HTTP messages for personally identifiable information, but learning based detectors need scarce hand labeled traffic. They also bind tightly to one fixed label taxonomy, so they transfer poorly when definitions of personal data shift across domains or over time.

Their pipeline supplies the taxonomy at runtime instead of baking it into training. Deterministic preprocessing feeds label level classification, targeted value labeling, and output checking stages run by language models. A tool creates synthetic traffic with validated labels, avoiding sensitive real captures for evaluation and prompting examples. Across three label sets of varied scope, the pipeline detected personal data types well and extracted the matching values.
arxiv-2605-06405:
Nam Anh Le studies market making for perpetual contracts on decentralized exchanges, where the funding rate moves as a random state variable. Holding inventory creates two linked effects: price exposure and a funding cash flow that depends on the position. Le turns that coupling into a reduced control problem.

The problem is solved with a monotone finite-difference method for a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, and quotes are recovered from value differences. Funding is calibrated on Hyperliquid data for ETH, BTC, and SOL. In holdout simulations the funding-aware method improves mean ETH and BTC results and lowers inventory risk, though the SOL gains are more mixed.
arxiv-2605-06905:
Eshed Gal, Md Shahriar Rahim Siddiqui, Moshe Eliasof, and Eldad Haber propose Conservative Flows, a generative modeling idea that starts from data instead of noise. Standard models transport random noise into samples through a learned flow. Conservative Flows instead run a step-by-step random dynamics that leaves the data distribution unchanged, seeded from data states, and can wrap around any trained flow model as its engine.

Two probability-preserving samplers are built: a corrected Langevin scheme with a Metropolis accept-reject step, and a predictor-corrector flow. Both run directly on existing checkpoints. On a spiral test target, ImageNet, and a flower dataset, the samplers steadily improve over the original generation methods they build on.
arxiv-2605-07305:
Hsin-Ling Hsu and eleven co-authors train medical language models to diagnose actively, the way doctors work in practice. Most model testing is done with complete information given at once, unlike real practice, where doctors order tests and update their thinking over turns. The team finds three common failures: ungrounded test choices, weak updates, and fading coherence.

Their MedAction pipeline builds multi-turn case dialogues through model-environment interaction, filtered by two knowledge-graph metrics for consistency. The resulting dataset holds tens of thousands of such records from thousands of published cases. A fine-tuned open model reached leading open-source results on two testing benchmarks, pushing active testing forward.
arxiv-2605-07505:
Yubin Wu and six co-authors train lightweight agents that operate graphical interfaces through long, branching tasks. Small GUI agents struggle because several different actions can be valid at each state, and fixed demonstrations ignore that freedom. LiteGUI trains on logged interface states with teacher guidance that picks the best-matching valid action at each step.

A second stage mixes action-level supervision with planning-quality supervision, still respecting multiple valid actions. A scalable pipeline produced a matching multi-solution dataset for training and evaluation.
